__comment: Firestore refuses a composite query with no matching index rather than running
it slowly, so a missing one is a hard failure the first time a filter is used —
not a gradual slowdown nobody notices. Declaring them here keeps that failure
out of production; the console's error also links to a one-click creation page
Single-field queries need nothing: the console's inbox is ordered by
lastMessageAt alone, and Firestore indexes every field on its own by default.

indexes.__comment: The widget, and findOpenForUser: one customer's newest thread.
findOpenForUser, which narrows to the open one before ordering.
The server-rendered inbox, filtered to open conversations.
The server-rendered inbox, filtered to one operator's threads.

__comment: The userId clause is not a filter anybody asked for — every message in the
subcollection already belongs to the one customer. It is there because the
security rule for a customer reads resource.data.userId, and Firestore
refuses a query it cannot prove is entirely readable rather than filtering
it. Without the clause the listener is denied; with it, this index.
The operator's listener over the same subcollection needs neither, because
isOperator() never looks at the document.
